A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Tok-RAG work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original QA experiments, token-level classification results, computational-cost measurements, mechanism analyses, and a layer-selection ablation.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds practical generation evaluations across additional tasks in Table 2.

M1.justification: Tok-RAG retains parallel LLM/RAG decoding, dynamic layer selection, retrieval-distribution estimation, and cosine-based token selection in Equations 14–19. The added prefix-update explanation describes behavior already shown in v2's Figure 1 and Appendix J.

E1.justification: v3 adds WoW dialogue, CodeXGLUE Python/Java generation, T-REx slot filling, and ELI5 long-form QA. It also adds sequence-generation evaluation on WikiText-103, previously evaluated through token-level benefit–detriment classification. Earlier benchmark coverage remains in the results.

E2.justification: Practical comparisons retain Standard RAG, NLI+RAG, CRAG, RetRobust, Self-RAG, and INFO-RAG; the added tasks reuse this set. Token-level comparisons retain Logprobs, Uncertainty, Consistency-Lexical, and Consistency-Semantic.

E3.justification: The added evaluations introduce F1, CodeBLEU, accuracy, and ROUGE-L protocols with LLaMA-2-7B. Appendix I specifies top-five retrieval for code, slot filling, and language modeling; SCODE-R over deduplicated CodeSearchNET for code; and supplied distractor contexts for WoW/ELI5. Retained experiments have no reported protocol revision.

E4.justification: The retrieval-noise tests, layerwise mechanism analyses, dynamic-versus-fixed-layer ablation, and six case studies are retained. Figure 4 and its ablation discussion move from the main text to Appendix I.5 without new analysis.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains the same p-value threshold and significance markers. Neither version supplies new seed information, repeated-run uncertainty, or confidence intervals. The added Table 2 reports point estimates without introducing another statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: New Table 2 reports six result columns, with Tok-RAG highest throughout. For example, Tok-RAG versus INFO-RAG scores are 68.70 versus 65.91 on T-REx accuracy and 27.44 versus 26.75 on Python CodeBLEU. Earlier QA, classification, cost, mechanism, ablation, and case-study results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Although Theorems 1–3 remain, v3 extends the formal analysis: Assumption 2 adds p(d|h_d,z)=1, Equations 5 and 23 correct equality to proportionality, and Appendix B expands the derivations. Appendix E introduces a claimed maximum-error rate sqrt(Upsilon)/exp(Upsilon), a substantive quantitative guarantee absent from v2.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims about distribution fusion, predicting token-level benefit versus detriment, and training-free collaborative generation. Condensing the contribution bullets does not remove their substantive claims.

C2.justification: Appendix E newly interprets larger detriment as making the theoretical approximation more robust. v3 removes the explicit limitation that 33B/65B models were not evaluated, although no such evaluations are added, and drops the earlier caveat about objectively evaluating long-form factual correctness.

D1.justification: v3 adds a Tok-RAG code-access link and task-specific retrieval, corpus, and context-count details in Appendix I. Existing hardware, framework, model, and decoding disclosures remain. However, explicit descriptions and source citations for ASQA/Bio/NQ and the ablation's model specification are lost.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including Rabiner's HMM tutorial, RegaVAE, and sources for new datasets and metrics, while removing several retained-dataset references and Jin et al. 2024b. The central positioning relative to robust RAG and theoretical ICL research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds a preliminary definitions-and-assumptions subsection, expands proof explanations, reorganizes experimental details, and relocates the ablation. It also condenses contribution bullets and updates publication, affiliation, and acknowledgment text. Most existing exposition and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 2, adjusts main-table sizing and caption placement, and relocates Figure 4 to the appendix. Existing cost and mechanism tables are renumbered. The other figures retain their content with modest layout changes.

improvement.justification: Table 2 broadens practical validation, while clearer preliminaries, retrieval details, and a code link improve accessibility. However, Appendix E's new error-rate formula increases for 0<Upsilon<1/2, contradicting its unqualified claim of decreasing error with greater detriment. Removal of the large-model limitation and some experimental descriptions also reduces transparency. These gains and weaknesses, particularly in a theory-centered paper, do not establish a reliable net quality improvement.
